intro: Two ways to join a clause you didn't expect: ～のに adds surprise or frustration, while ～けど is a plain, conversational 'but'.

grammar.title: ～のに and ～けど

rules.label: Verbs & い-adjectives
rules.detail: Attach to the plain form (present or past).
examples: 行く → 行くのに / 行くけど (even though/but I go)
高い → 高いのに / 高いけど (even though/but it's expensive)

rules.label: な-adjectives & nouns
rules.detail: のに takes な; けど keeps だ.
examples: べんり → べんりなのに / べんりだけど
学生 → 学生なのに / 学生だけど

rules.label: ～のに
rules.detail: 'Even though / and yet' — carries emotion: surprise, disappointment, complaint.
examples: 高いのに、おいしくない → Even though it's pricey, it's not good (grr)

rules.label: ～けど
rules.detail: 'But / although' — neutral contrast, like が but conversational; can follow polite form too.
examples: 行きますけど → but I'll go

grammar.bigPoint: Use のに only when the second clause states a fact or feeling — never a request, command, or invitation. For those, switch to けど: 近いけど、歩きましょう。

examples.jp: たかいのに、おいしくない。
examples.en: Even though it's expensive, it's not tasty.

examples.jp: えきは ちかいけど、バスで 行きます。
examples.romaji: Eki wa chikai kedo, basu de ikimasu.
examples.en: The station is close, but I'll go by bus.

examples.jp: よやくしたのに、せきが なかった。
examples.romaji: Yoyaku shita noni, seki ga nakatta.
examples.en: Even though I made a reservation, there were no seats.

note: のに often ends a sentence on its own as a soft complaint — 予約したのに…！ ('But I made a reservation…!'). Remember the な after a な-adjective or noun before のに (べんりなのに), but だ before けど (べんりだけど).

selfCheck.q: How would you say: "Even though it's convenient, it's expensive."
selfCheck.a: べんりなのに、たかいです。 (Benri na noni, takai desu.) — note the な after べんり before のに.
